1

The present claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .30,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 26.07.2024 at about 08.30 p.m., when he was walking on left side of the road while going to Magadi - Bengaluru Main Road, Opp Janaseva School,
Channenahalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru City, a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-41- ES-9614, ridden by its rider at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to him.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to Kenganar Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Plaster Work and earning .30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of notice, both the respondents appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondents have denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondents also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondents contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the accident has not taken place on account of any rashness or negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
Further respondent No.1 contended that they are the Registered owner of the motor cycle Regn.No.KA-41-ES-9614 and records pertaining to the said motor vehicle are standing in their name.

Further, the said motor vehicle is insured with the second respondent under policy vide No.3005/5434139/10104/000 which was valid from 25.01.2024 to 24.01.2025 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.

Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.
5.

Respondent No.2, in the written statement, contended that the Motor cycle stood insured with them as on the date of accident vide policy No.3005/54341339/10104/000 valid from 25.01.2024 to 24.01.2025 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further this respondent has issued a policy to motor cycle.
Further the motor cycle was not at all involved in the accident and the driver of alleged vehicle was in no way related in the cause of alleged accident as on the date of accident.
Further the rider of motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.

Hence,
prayed for dismissal of petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following:

1. Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 26.07.2024 at about 08.30 p.m., when petitioner was going to the Magadi-Bengaluru Main Road, on left side of the road, when reached opp to Janaseva School Channenahalli, Tavarekere Hobli, Bengaluru South, Bengaluru City, due to the rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ES-9614 by its rider?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award?

7. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got examined Dr.Ramesh.B., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 and closed evidence of his side.

On the other hand,
the respondent insurance company got examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked one document at Ex.R.1 and closed their side of evidence.

8. Heard the argument of both the side and perused the materials available on record.
9.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:-

11.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, it discloses that one of the relatives of petitioner by name Sri.Shambulinga S/o Late Sharanappa has lodged complaint with police on 27.07.2024 with respect to the accident occurred on 26.07.2024.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s 125(a), 281 of BNS.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of offending vehicle by its rider.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.1 discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the rider of offending motor cycle.

. PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
17. On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and got marked one document at Ex.R.1.
The evidence of RW.1 is not of much assistance to the respondents in order to substantiate their contention and to disprove the contention of petitioner.
It is the contention of respondents that the petitioner was also negligent in the cause of accident as he was walking on the road.
But, no satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show the aspect of negligence exhibited by petitioner in the cause of accident.
Neither the petitioner nor respondents furnished sketch before the Tribunal in order ascertain the aspect of negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of the vehicle, is proper person to state about involvement of offending vehicle and negligence on the part of petitioner or rider of motorcycle.
But, except filing the written statement, respondent No.1 not examined any witness on their behalf in order to disprove the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle.
The materials placed on record disclose the aspect negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record are not sufficient and satisfactory to ascertain the aspect of negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.
The respondents not placed cogent and substantive materials in order to substantiate their contention.
18. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of record, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.9, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-41-ES-9614 by its rider and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:
The petitioner succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc., in order to assess the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.

sentences.text: The said document discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner also furnished discharge summary which is marked as Ex.P.8 and he said document discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner for the injuries sustained by his in the accident.
Further, the petitioner examined Dr.Ramesh.B., as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P14 & 15 documents.
PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability to the right Lower limb at 46% and to whole body at 23%.
On consideration of the materials placed before the Tribunal, compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards Pain and Suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at the Hospital for which he incurred expenses.
The petitioner has produced medical bills amounting to .1,34,663/- marked at Ex.P.10 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.11 and receipts marked at Ex.P.12.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.

So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .1,34,663/-
appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:- On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 26.07.2024 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.
On perusal of materials on record
, the petitioner appears to have admitted as an inpatient at Hospital pertaining to the injuries sustained by him and availed treatment as an inpatient.

So,
during the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.8, Discharge Summary issued by Kenganar Hospital, which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner as an inpatient from 26.07.2024 to 30.07.2024 i.e., for a period of 05 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 05 days to a sum of .2,500/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:-
The petitioner is the resident of Chitapur Kalaburgi, Karnataka and he has admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.8.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses for conveyance during the period of treatment.

Considering the injuries sustained and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/-
appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might have not attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.

(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:-
The petitioner contended that due to the accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner examined Dr.Ramesh.B working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria, Bengaluru as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained Grade II compound both bone lower 1/3rd, right leg comminuted fracture and underwent wound debridement internal fixation of fibula external fixation after underwent removal of external fixation and later discharged.

Further petitioner complains of pain in right leg,
difficulty to squat on floor sit cross legged climb upstairs walk on slope kneel stand on affected limb and difficulty to do routine activities.

Further PW.2 deposed that on examination found disabilities restriction of joint movement of right ankle plantardorsiflexio of 60, normal 0.70, difficulty to squat on the floor, climb upstairs,
walk on slope kneel sit cross legged stand on affected limb and difficulty to do routine activities.
Further as per radiological examination shows fracture fibula with implants in situ, fracture tibia mal united.
The doctor has assessed the disability to the right lower limb at 46% and to the whole body at 23%.

In order to prove his disability, the doctor has produced Clinical notes and X-ray marked at Ex.P.14 & 15.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.

Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,500/- x 12) = .1,98,000/-
 Loss of future earning p.a. (10% of prior annual  income) = .19,800/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 17 Loss of future earnings - (.19,800/- x 17) = .3,36,600/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .3,36,600/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:-
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable to do his day- today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.2 has opined that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implants, but they have not mentioned the estimation of cost for this surgery.
No materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to show the expenses that may incurred for future surgery for removal implants.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .25,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.
